To further assess the therapeutic relevance of this TGF-β1-associated cell state, we pharmacologically blocked TGF-β signaling in patient-derived tumor-like clusters, which increased IFN-γ and GZMB expression, consistent with enhanced immune cytotoxicity. Together, these findings highlight the TGF-β1-associated fibroblast-like malignant program as potential therapeutic vulnerabilities in MESO.

title: Perioperative blood staging based on personalized ctDNA assay for recurrence prediction in NSCLC
abstract: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is a valuable biomarker for relapse monitoring. However, current personalized approaches are unable to detect emerging clones, and perioperative ctDNA dynamics remain to be defined. We prospectively validated Hi-SECURE, a tumour-informed MRD assay, in 132 NSCLC patients (POEM cohort). Analytical performance was benchmarked against reference standards and a fixed 158-gene panel. A perioperative blood (PB) staging system was proposed and externally validated. Hi-SECURE achieves a limit of detection of 0.005% with a DNA input of 20 ng. At the landmark time point, ctDNA positivity predicted recurrence with a hazard ratio (HR) of 17.14 (95% CI: 3.06–96.11). Hi‑SECURE outperformed the fixed panel, especially in stage IA (25.0% vs 6.8% detection rate, p = 0.020). Pre‑ and postoperative ctDNA status enabled PB staging, which showed strong prognostic discrimination (log rank p < 0.001), was validated across external cohorts. Moreover, Hi-SECURE’s core panel identified drug-resistant mutations (e.g., EGFR -T790M) during follow-up, enabling timely therapeutic adjustments. In conclusion, Hi‑SECURE is a highly sensitive and specific personalized MRD assay. The proposed PB staging system provides a functional, dynamic complement to anatomical TNM staging, enabling precise prognostic stratification and offering potential guidance for adjuvant therapy, resistance monitoring, and immunotherapy candidate selection.

title: Establishment and characterization of primary retinoblastoma cell lines: a comprehensive molecular profiling approach
abstract: Retinoblastoma (RB) research is significantly constrained by the limited availability of preclinical models that accurately recapitulate the disease complexity, particularly regarding the context of vitreous seeding, a major driver of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Here, we report the establishment and integrative characterization of patient-derived, three-dimensional (3D) spheroid models generated from primary retinal tumors (RBT) and vitreous seeds (RBVS). Across a cohort of 10 cell lines generated from 8 eyes and 8 patients, both RBT and RBVS models demonstrated sustained 3D growth and preserved key phenotypic features of the original tumors. Genome-wide DNA methylation and copy number profiling revealed strong concordance between primary tumors and derived models, supporting their molecular fidelity. RB1 inactivation was identified as the founding driver event, while additional alterations, including BCOR loss-of-function mutations and MYCN , ALK , and IKBKE amplifications, defined clinically aggressive subsets and were retained in corresponding models. Comparative analyses of matched samples showed that 3D spheroid generated models maintain core oncogenic drivers. Collectively, our data establish patient-derived 3D RB models as robust and translationally relevant platforms that recapitulate tumor heterogeneity and evolution. These systems provide a valuable resource for biomarker discovery, mechanistic investigation of resistance pathways, and development of precision therapeutic strategies in RB.

title: System biology analysis reveals circadian rhythm disorder associated with development and progression in colorectal cancer
abstract: Circadian rhythm disorders represent an abstract concept lacking standardized quantitative metrics. Existing circadian indicators, including traditional rhythm parameters and a limited set of clock gene or physiological biomarkers, are insufficient to robustly capture steady-state endogenous circadian homeostasis in complex disease contexts, thereby constraining quantitative assessment of circadian disruption and limiting its translational applicability. Chronic circadian rhythm disruption is associated with various diseases, including metabolic disorders and malignancies. However, the mechanisms by which circadian disruption influences tumor microenvironment formation and colorectal cancer progression remain incompletely understood. This study employs systems biology analysis to decipher the molecular characteristics of circadian rhythm disruption in colorectal cancer progression. We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 13 CRC tissue samples and 12 normal mucosal samples, combined with 3733 samples from 34 public batch RNA, microarray, and single-cell RNA sequencing cohorts. We developed and validated the ClockProCRC system, which detects and quantifies intrinsic circadian misalignment in CRC. The ClockProCRC score elucidates how circadian misalignment drives CRC progression trajectories, shapes clinical phenotypes, regulates disease manifestations, and reshapes the tumor microenvironment. SYNE1 gene was identified as a key mediator of circadian misalignment, promoting tumorigenesis by driving epithelial-like phenotypic conversion and demonstrating therapeutic potential in colorectal cancer management. This study establishes a foundation for integrating rhythmic information into clinical practice and advances circadian biology research in the field of CRC.

title: Integrated genomic and transcriptomic profiling across the clinical spectrum of Lynch syndrome-associated endometrial disease
abstract: We investigated the molecular processes underlying the clinical spectrum of Lynch syndrome (LS)-associated endometrial disease using integrated genomic and transcriptomic profiling of endometrial tissues. Whole-transcriptome sequencing revealed distinct patterns of immune remodeling across clinically defined disease states (unaffected carrier, premalignant, and malignant states), characterized by increasing infiltration of T cells, particularly CD8+ subsets and B cells. Non-negative matrix factorization of transcriptomic profiles identified two cancer-associated features and one feature enriched in normal endometrium, with validation in external datasets. A dominant cancer-associated feature was characterized by immune activation, effector T-cells, and exhaustion-associated CD8+ T-cell transcriptional signatures, consistent with an immune-active microenvironment. Whole-exome sequencing identified oncogenic mutations and mismatch repair deficiency –associated mutational signatures in premalignant lesions, suggesting that these alterations are already detectable in premalignant lesions within the LS disease spectrum. Together, these findings suggest distinct immune and genomic alterations across the clinical spectrum of LS-associated endometrial disease, providing molecular insights that may inform future biomarker development and prevention-oriented studies in high-risk individuals.

title: Artificial intelligence for microsatellite instability detection in precision oncology: a systematic review from 2015 to 2025
abstract: Microsatellite instability (MSI) and mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR) are clinically actionable biomarkers that guide immunotherapy selection and prognostic stratification across multiple solid tumors. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR), immunohistochemistry (IHC), and next-generation sequencing (NGS) remain reference standards for MSI/dMMR assessment. We conducted a systematic review of artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches for MSI/dMMR detection, searching PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Springer, and ScienceDirect for studies first publicly available between January 2015 and December 2025. Study selection followed PRISMA guidelines, and risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Of 1589 records, 111 studies were included after full-text review, hierarchically sorted by validation strategy (prioritizing independent external validation), cohort size, and performance metrics. AI-based prediction has been evaluated across histopathology whole-slide images (WSIs), radiology, omics, endoscopy, clinical variables, and multimodal combinations. Deep learning applied to H&E WSIs is the most extensively studied approach, although external validation remains inconsistent. Multimodal models are promising, but superiority over single-modality models remains unproven. Most studies predict assay-defined MSI/dMMR rather than treatment outcomes; the available evidence does not yet support routine clinical use of AI for triage or assay replacement. Prospective multicenter trials should evaluate AI-derived phenotypes as complementary or standalone biomarkers for treatment selection.

title: Genetically engineered dendritic cells in cancer immunotherapy: from immune reprogramming strategies to emerging CAR-DC platforms
abstract: Genetic engineering can enhance dendritic cell (DC) migration, antigen presentation, co-stimulation, cytokine production, survival, and resistance to tumor-mediated suppression. This review examines established engineering strategies and emerging chimeric antigen receptor-engineered DCs (CAR-DCs). Preclinical studies indicate that CAR-DCs may promote tumor-material uptake, cross-presentation, T cell priming, and microenvironmental remodeling. However, limited persistence, manufacturing complexity, safety uncertainties, and the absence of clinical outcome data remain major barriers to translation.

title: Driver gene-based prognostic model benchmarked against machine learning survival models is associated with a CAF–TGFβ–EMT-like phenotype in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is molecularly heterogeneous, limiting conventional prognostic tools. Whole-genome resequencing of six HCC cases was used only to filter candidates. Somatically mutated genes were intersected with HCC-annotated entries from five predefined driver resources, yielding 154 genes. DGPM-HCC, a 13-gene model summarized by TotalScore, was developed in 170 bulk transcriptome samples. In 20 repetitions of event-stratified fivefold cross-validation, DGPM-HCC achieved a mean overall-survival C-index of 0.761; versus continuous Cox13, the median paired ΔC-index was 0.125 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.111–0.142; P = 9.57 × 10 −5 ). The combined nomogram achieved a training-cohort 3-year disease-free-survival AUC of 0.924. External discrimination in TCGA-LIHC was modest (C-index, 0.533; 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUCs, 0.503, 0.592, and 0.590), whereas GSE14520 lacked three model genes. Exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing of one tumor–adjacent pair, public single-cell integration, and multiplex immunohistochemistry on 16 specimens associated high TotalScore with a CAF–TGFβ–EMT-like state. Drug-sensitivity findings were computational and exploratory.

title: PLAU orchestrates pancreatic cancer progression via PI3K/AKT/mTORC1-mediated upregulation of MMP2/9 and FSCN1
abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) is a highly lethal malignancy. PLAU is upregulated in multiple cancers and contributes to tumor progression. Nevertheless, the precise function and molecular mechanism of PLAU in PC progression remain unclear. This study confirmed that PLAU is markedly upregulated in PC and correlated with advanced stage and poor prognosis. PLAU knockdown suppressed PC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and invadopodia formation and inhibited tumor growth and lung metastasis in vivo. Transcriptomic data from PC tissues and single-cell sequencing showed a significant positive association between PLAU and mTORC1 signaling, MMP2/9, and FSCN1. qRT-PCR and western blot indicated that PLAU knockdown downregulated PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 signaling activity and reduced MMP2/9 and FSCN1 expression, while PLAU overexpression exerted opposite effects. The mTORC1 signaling inhibitor WRX606 reversed PLAU overexpression-mediated upregulation of MMP2/9 and FSCN1. Patient-derived pancreatic cancer organoids (PDPCOs) further validated that PLAU knockdown downregulated mTORC1 signaling, MMP2/9, and FSCN1 and impaired the development and growth of PDPCOs. Collectively, this study revealed that PLAU promotes PC progression by activating PI3K/AKT/mTORC1 signaling to upregulate MMP2/9 and FSCN1, elucidating the specific molecular mechanism by which PLAU drives PC progression and laying the groundwork for further developing novel therapeutic targets and approaches against PC.

title: Patient-derived organoids enable ex vivo drug-response profiling for precision medicine in bladder cancer
abstract: Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) represent a promising precision medicine approach for replicating primary tumor characteristics and facilitating drug testing across various cancers, although clinical evidence in bladder cancer remains limited. This study evaluates the impact of incorporating PDOs into clinical practice on treatment efficacy in bladder cancer patients. Surgical specimens were used to establish PDOs, which were systematically characterized and compared to parental tumors in terms of histological morphology and genomic features. Based on standard clinical regimens, customized drug combinations were designed for ex vivo drug-response profiling, and the resultant profiles were correlated with individual patients’ clinical responses. Nineteen bladder cancer PDOs were successfully established with an 86.4% success rate, and they closely resembled the parental tumors histopathologically and genetically. Drug sensitivity screening was performed for chemotherapy agents and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) using the established PDOs, and the results revealed individual heterogeneity among patients. In an exploratory cohort, ex vivo PDO drug-response profiles were concordant with postoperative clinical outcomes in 9 of 10 evaluable patients (90.0%), supporting the potential clinical relevance of PDO-based drug-response profiling. This study establishes a bladder cancer organoid biobank and highlights the potential of this platform to support personalized treatment strategies and precision medicine in bladder cancer.

title: Transarterial infusion chemotherapy and embolization as a novel neoadjuvant therapy for locally advanced gastric cancer: a prospective single-arm pilot study
abstract: Currently, there is limited evidence for the application of interventional therapy in the treatment of hollow viscera tumors. This prospective, single-arm, pilot study (NCT05396326) evaluated the efficacy and safety profile of transarterial infusion chemotherapy and embolization (TAICE) as a novel pre-operative treatment for locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC) and explored its potential anti-tumor mechanisms. Twenty patients were enrolled in this study. The pathological complete response (pCR) and major pathological response (MPR) rates were 55.0% and 70.0%, respectively, and the safety profile was manageable. Patients with lower tumor residual rates showed a lower risk of recurrence, and angiographic tumor feeding artery patterns showed an association with postoperative progression-free survival. Exploratory spatial transcriptomic analyses suggested that TAICE may be associated with enhanced endoplasmic reticulum stress, altered tumor epithelial cell states, and increased intercellular communication within the tumor microenvironment. Overall, these preliminary findings suggest that TAICE may represent a complementary pre-operative locoregional strategy for selected patients with LAGC, especially those with branching tumor feeding arteries. Further investigation in prospective controlled trials with larger sample sizes is necessary.

title: Neo-BCV induces macrophage-associated immunometabolic remodeling and anti-tumor immunity in solid tumors
abstract: Immunotherapy targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis has transformed cancer treatment; however, limited response rates and therapeutic resistance remain major challenges. Here, we developed a novel multi-component inactivated bacterial complex vaccine (Neo-BCV) to enhance anti-tumor efficacy by reprogramming innate immune responses. Neo-BCV significantly suppressed tumor growth without inducing systemic toxicity and remodeled the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting macrophage infiltration and polarization toward an M1-like phenotype while reducing M2-like TAMs. These changes were associated with enhanced CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, effector memory phenotype, and cytokine production. Mechanistically, Neo-BCV activated NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling and induced metabolic and inflammatory reprogramming in macrophages. Macrophage depletion partially impaired Neo-BCV-mediated tumor control, indicating an important role for macrophages in the anti-tumor activity of Neo-BCV. Importantly, Neo-BCV demonstrated anti-tumor efficacy in additional MC38 and Hepa1-6 subcutaneous tumor models, accompanied by enhanced M1-like macrophage polarization and CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration. Furthermore, in a registered clinical study (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05747339; registered February 16, 2023) involving 27 patients with advanced solid tumors, Neo-BCV demonstrated a disease control rate of 77.78% with a favorable safety profile. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Neo-BCV reshapes the tumor immune microenvironment through macrophage activation and enhances adaptive anti-tumor immunity. Its preclinical anti-tumor activity, together with a trend toward improved tumor control when combined with immune checkpoint blockade, and preliminary clinical activity support further evaluation of Neo-BCV as a potential immunotherapeutic strategy for solid tumors.

title: Multidimensional immune subtyping reveals clinicogenetic molecular functional and pharmacologic heterogeneity in acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is characterized by substantial immune heterogeneity, yet current disease classification is dominated by cytogenetic and molecular features and does not systematically incorporate the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Here, we developed an AML-specific TIME classification based on 1503 curated immune-related genes and identified five immune subtypes (IS1–IS5) with distinct clinical, molecular, immunologic, and pharmacologic features. The subtype structure was established in GEO datasets and further evaluated in TCGA-LAML and Beat AML. TIME subtype was associated with survival, FAB morphology, ELN risk, mutational patterns, and established HOX–MEIS, NPM1-associated, and FLT3-ITD transcriptional programs, while remaining only partially explained by these conventional AML features. In Beat AML, addition of TIME subtype to age, sex, and ELN2017 significantly improved prognostic model fit and modestly increased discrimination, supporting its value as a complementary immune layer for risk assessment. Immune profiling identified IS4 as the most immune-engaged subtype, whereas IS1 and IS5 displayed relatively immune-low or exclusion-prone states. Projection of the pembrolizumab-treated GSE183415 cohort further supported the immunotherapy relevance of this immune-state axis. Importantly, primary AML samples provided functional validation: IS4 showed higher CD274, HLA-DRA, CXCL9, CXCL10, and LGALS9 expression, increased PD-L1/HLA-DR positivity, enhanced T-cell-mediated blast killing, and greater CD8 + T-cell activation compared with IS1. Beat AML drug-screen analysis additionally revealed subtype-specific ex vivo drug sensitivities, several of which persisted after adjustment for ELN2017. These findings establish a multidimensional AML TIME framework that complements existing clinicogenetic classification and provides a basis for refined immune stratification, prognostic assessment, and subtype-informed therapeutic investigation.

title: Circulating and spatial immune biomarkers of response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and nivolumab in ER + /HER2- breast cancer: analysis of the phase II GIADA trial
abstract: Adding an ICI to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) increases pCR rates in ER+/HER2- high-risk BC, but also toxicity, highlighting the need for predictive biomarkers. We explored associations between circulating immune-mediators, spatial tumor immune architecture, and pCR in the phase II GIADA trial. Forty-three premenopausal patients with stage II–IIIA ER+/HER2− Luminal B-like BC received epirubicin-cyclophosphamide x3 followed by nivolumab and endocrine treatment. Plasma levels of 47 circulating immune-mediators were evaluated at baseline (t0), after chemotherapy (t1), and before surgery (t2). Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed on tumor biopsies at t0 and t1 to assess spatial interactions between cell subpopulations. At baseline, seven immune-mediators were significantly higher in pCR-patients: IFNγ, GROα, sCD40L, EGF, VEGF-A, PDGF-AA, PDGF-AB/B. A composite 7-cytokine score was significantly associated with pCR (OR 3.04, p = 0.017). These immune-mediators were positively associated with infiltration by specific immune cell subpopulations, including tumoral/stromal PD-L1+ macrophages and PD-1+ T-cells, and intratumoral CD4+ and CD8+GranzymeB+ cells. At baseline, spatial interactions between tumor cells and multiple immune subpopulations (CD4+, CD8+, FOXP3+ T-cells and CD68+ macrophages) were associated with pCR. At t1, interactions involving CD8+GranzymeB+ T-cells were more prominent among responders. Circulating immune-mediators and tumor-immune spatial organization are associated with pCR in high-risk ER+/HER2− BC treated with chemoimmunotherapy.

title: Prediction of site-specific recurrence and overall survival for colorectal cancer with liver metastases
abstract: Up to 70% of patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM) experience recurrence after curative-intent hepatectomy, yet recurrence patterns are heterogeneous across anatomic sites, and no tools currently exist to predict site-specific recurrence dynamically over time. We developed and validated machine learning models to predict overall survival and site-specific recurrence (liver, lung, lymph node, peritoneum) after hepatectomy for CRLM using baseline and dynamic prediction frameworks. In a retrospective cohort of 730 patients who underwent curative-intent hepatectomy for CRLM at the Johns Hopkins Hospital (2000–2024), with a median follow-up of 10.9 years, over 63% of patients experienced recurrence. XGBoost models were trained on clinical, pathologic, and molecular features using nested cross-validation with bootstrap optimism correction. Baseline models achieved C-indices of 0.54–0.67, while dynamic models incorporating surveillance covariates, including adjuvant therapy and interval recurrence at other sites, substantially improved discrimination (C-indices 0.67–0.78; time-dependent AUC 0.68–0.90). Calibration was confirmed with Brier scores of 0.03–0.19. These models enable risk stratification at the time of surgery to inform adjuvant therapy decisions and allow real-time updating of site-specific recurrence risk during follow-up, providing a framework for personalized surveillance strategies in patients with CRLM undergoing curative-intent resection.

title: Decoding drug-tolerant persister states in cancer: insights from single-cell, spatial, and computational approaches
abstract: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have transformed oncogene-driven cancer treatment, but durable responses remain limited by residual disease and acquired resistance. Drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells represent one therapy-surviving component of minimal residual disease (MRD). This Review examines experimental and computational strategies, including patient-derived xenografts, CRISPR screens, single-cell, spatial, multi-omic and artificial intelligence approaches, to define DTP states, MRD heterogeneity, microenvironmental interactions and clinically actionable vulnerabilities with greater resolution in TKI-treated cancers.

title: Author Correction: Microbiome and biofilm insights from normal vs tumor tissues in Thai colorectal cancer patients
Patient-derived vascularized organoid-on-a-chip model for therapeutic response assessment in synovial sarcoma
abstract: Synovial sarcoma (SS) lacks effective therapies and physiologically relevant models that faithfully recapitulate the tumor microenvironment. Here, we established synovial sarcoma patient-derived organoids (SPDOs) that preserved the histological, genomic, and transcriptomic features of their parental tumors. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of paired pre- and post-treatment tumors revealed increased treatment-associated transcriptional remodeling of malignant cells, vascular remodeling, and disruption of tumor-stromal communication following chemotherapy and anti-angiogenic therapy. Guided by these findings, we incorporated cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and endothelial cells to generate stromal-vascular SPDOs and subsequently established a vascularized SPDO-on-a-chip (VSC) model capable of supporting perfusable vascular networks. Anlotinib markedly disrupted vascular architecture, while the VSC model exhibited distinct drug-response profiles compared with conventional organoids, highlighting the importance of incorporating stromal and endothelial components into preclinical drug evaluation. In a representative clinical case, ex vivo drug responses in the VSC model were concordant with the observed response to doxorubicin-based chemotherapy and anlotinib treatment. In addition, targeted drug testing demonstrated that pazopanib and vorinostat differentially modulated immune-related pathways and SS18-SSX-associated transcriptional programs. Collectively, the VSC model provides a scalable and physiologically relevant platform for studying tumor-vascular interactions and supporting therapeutic response assessment in SS.

title: Decoding spatial mTOR signalling reveals distinct roles in the tumour microenvironment
abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in different tissue compartments influences patient prognosis. We found that mTOR pathway signalling in immune cells correlates with favourable patient survival. Advanced spatially-aware analysis of signalling activities using graph neural networks revealed that the positive association between immune mTOR signalling and patient survival was more pronounced in tumours with features of a more differentiated morphology. Integrative analysis using TCGA data and spatial transcriptomics confirmed a role for immune mTOR signalling in immune activation, accompanied by reduced TGF-β signalling. Our work highlights the importance of adopting a personalised approach to targeting mTOR in cancer patients and establishes a framework for studying cell type-specific signalling in the TME.

title: MYBL2 amplification and expression associate with mitotic activation and prognostic divergence in uterine leiomyosarcoma
abstract: Uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) is an aggressive gynecologic malignancy with limited treatment options. MYBL2, a master regulator of cell-cycle progression, is implicated in several cancers but poorly defined in uLMS. Using multi-omics profiling of 87 fresh-frozen uterine tissues, an integrated mRNA cohort of 201 samples, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) in 133 gynecologic tumors, we show that MYBL2 is focally amplified at 20q13.12 in 30% of uLMS and overexpressed at the mRNA level across cohorts. MYBL2-high tumors show activation of DNA-replication and mitotic pathways, coordinated upregulation of protein targets (CDK1, BIRC5, KPNA2, CCNB1, KIF20A), and an immune-cold microenvironment. Despite consistent mRNA elevation, MYBL2 protein was only sporadically detected, and within the active MMB/DREAM program MYBL2 and FOXM1 were the least-detectable proteins, indicating post-transcriptional suppression of the regulators. Higher MYBL2 mRNA and MMB/DREAM transcriptional activity were associated with shorter overall survival (continuous HR = 4.3 per SD, p = 0.001), whereas higher MYBL2 protein by IHC was associated with longer survival (HR = 0.79, p = 0.046). MYBL2 amplification and overexpression thus define a proliferative, immune-cold, poor-prognosis uLMS subset, with a notable transcript–protein prognostic discordance.

title: ANGPTL4 is a hypoxia associated candidate linked to immune and vascular phenotypes in ccRCC
abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by prominent vascularization and cellular heterogeneity, but reliable biomarkers for angiogenesis and response to targeted therapy remain limited. In this study, transcriptomic data from GEO cohorts (GSE53757, GSE66271, GSE73731) and two validation datasets (GSE36895, GSE66270) were analyzed using WGCNA and multiple machine learning models. ANGPTL4, together with GPC3, SCARB1, and ADM, was identified as a candidate gene set. ANGPTL4 showed good diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.857) and was positioned between angiogenesis- and lipid metabolism- related modules in the PPI network. Single-cell analysis indicated heterogeneous expression across epithelial and immune cells, and in silico knockout suggested enhanced T-cell–related signaling. ANGPTL4 was identified from a candidate set enriched for hypoxia-related genes and showed cell-type-specific expression in the single-cell dataset. In vitro, ANGPTL4 knockdown altered CCL5 secretion, NK-92-cell-associated phenotypes, and Matrigel network formation. These findings support an association of ANGPTL4 with hypoxia-related, immune, and vascular phenotypes in ccRCC; however, they do not establish direct mediation through the HIF–VEGF signaling axis.

title: LLM-based reconstruction of longitudinal clinical trajectories in chronic liver disease
abstract: Liver cancer primarily develops in patients with chronic liver disease (CLD), yet most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages with poor prognosis. While CLD surveillance generates extensive longitudinal data, its free-text nature hinders large-scale research. To address this, we developed a scalable framework using open-source LLMs with constrained decoding to process unstructured text across radiology, pathology, and transplant assessment domains. A calibration set comprising 507 reports from 30 patients was manually annotated to benchmark four LLMs against a regular expression baseline across 70 tasks. Llama-3.3-70B performed best, exceeding 90% accuracy on 59/70 tasks, outperforming Llama-3.1-8B (a smaller variant), OpenBioLLM-70B (a medically fine-tuned model), and DeepSeek-R1-8B. Constrained decoding achieved > 99.9% format adherence, far surpassing unconstrained prompting (87.4%). Applied to the full cohort, the pipeline analysed 22,493 reports to generate a patient-level database of 29,225 datapoints (35 variables, 835 patients) without manual annotation. Further analysis confirmed known liver cancer risk factors (male sex, viral hepatitis, smoking, diabetes), and allowed for reconstruction of individualised disease timelines. This work provides a scalable blueprint for transforming real-world clinical free-text into structured formats and personalised patient trajectories. Future applications have the potential to accelerate data-driven research into early cancer detection within complex pre-cancerous diseases like CLD.

title: Cost drivers of cancer sequencing technologies
abstract: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) is widely recommended for cancer diagnosis and monitoring, but is perceived as prohibitively expensive. Using Medicare reimbursement data and microcosting analysis in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we find that sequencing alone costs less than the ~$1000 reimbursement, while library preparation ($12–$154/sample), driven by oligonucleotide synthesis, comprises an increasing share of cost. Expanding NGS access may depend more on cheaper library preparation and systems-level centralization.

title: Prediction of outcomes and exploration of underlying mechanisms in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer after concurrent chemoradiotherapy
abstract: We aimed to construct nomograms combining clinical indicators, apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values, and MRI radiomics signatures to predict early therapeutic response, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) in locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC), and further uncover the biological basis of radiomics features. A total of 671 LACC patients from two centers were retrospectively enrolled and split into training ( n = 381) and external validation cohorts ( n = 290). LASSO regression screened radiomics features to calculate radiomics scores (Rad-scores), and multivariate Logistic/Cox regression was adopted to build three visualized prediction models, followed by internal and cross-institutional external validation. Bioinformatic analysis and immunohistochemistry were performed to explore underlying molecular mechanisms. All three nomograms achieved favorable discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit, with AUCs ranging from 0.828 to 0.951 in both cohorts. Radiomics signatures were predominantly enriched in DNA damage repair and cell cycle pathways, with LIG4 identified as the hub gene positively correlated with Rad-scores and significantly linked to unsatisfactory CCRT response and poor patient prognosis. The nomograms serve as non-invasive predictive tools for LACC patients receiving CCRT and can reflect activated tumor DNA damage repair mediated by LIG4, offering solid biological evidence for radiomics clinical translation.

title: MAVEN: an automated multimodal framework for predicting VETC and early recurrence in HCC
abstract: Accurate identification of aggressive tumor phenotypes remains a major challenge in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Here, we developed and validated MAVEN (Multimodal Automated VETC Estimation Network), a fully automated multimodal deep learning system integrating magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), whole-slide histopathology images (WSIs), and clinical variables for predicting vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) and early recurrence risk. In this multicenter study including 1928 patients from five institutions, MAVEN demonstrated superior performance compared with unimodal and bimodal models, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.932 in the internal test cohort and 0.879-0.891 across four independent external cohorts. MAVEN-based risk stratification was significantly associated with early recurrence-free survival across all cohorts. Model explainability analyses revealed that both radiologic and histopathologic features contributed to prediction, with consistent spatial localization of high-risk regions. These findings suggest that multimodal integration enables robust and generalizable prediction of tumor aggressiveness and postoperative risk stratification.

title: Combination strategy of photothermal therapy and targeted IFN-β mutein priming elicits a durable abscopal effect
abstract: Metastatic tumors remain difficult to cure due to frequent dissemination and recurrence. While photothermal therapy (PTT) can trigger abscopal effects, PTT monotherapy often fails to sustain systemic immunity. Here, we investigated a tripartite strategy combining PTT, a tumor-targeted type I interferon immunocytokine, and immune checkpoint blockade. Using an engineered claudin-3–targeted IFN-β mutein (CLDN3–IFN-βm) in human IFNAR1/2 knock-in mice, we found that combining PTT with CLDN3–IFN-βm synergistically reprogrammed the tumor microenvironment. This combination expanded activated dendritic cells in tumor-draining lymph nodes and enhanced CD8⁺ T cell infiltration into untreated distant tumors, thereby establishing durable immune memory. Crucially, this robust activation induced adaptive resistance through upregulation of the PD-1/PD-L1 axis. Accordingly, adding PD-1 blockade led to marked tumor regression and sustained systemic antitumor immunity, offering a potential curative strategy for metastatic solid tumors.

title: Prime editing reveals the resistance landscape of EGFR tyrosine kinase domain variants
abstract: Resistance of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) remains a major challenge in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Here, we used prime editing to profile 1676 single-amino-acid variants and 10 insertion variants of exon 20 across the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain against afatinib, dacomitinib, and osimertinib. In an L858R-based NSCLC model, we evaluated ~90% of all possible single-amino-acid variants and integrated these data with a published exon 19 deletion-based dataset to define a context-independent resistance profile, capturing 10,255 drug-variant combinations across two EGFR-activating contexts and revealing shared and context-specific resistance patterns. Benchmarking against curated clinical annotations and survival data enabled high-confidence classification of resistance and sensitivity to afatinib for ~86% of all possible variants, to dacomitinib for ~74%, and to osimertinib for ~82%. This study provides a clinically relevant resource of EGFR TKI resistance and a framework for variant profiling.

title: Retraction Note: Development of a stemness-related prognostic index to provide therapeutic strategies for bladder cancer
B-cell activating factor contributes to CAR-T cell-associated cytokine release syndrome
abstract: Cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is the most common and potentially life-threatening toxicity associated with CAR-T cell therapy and is related to a heightened immune effector state. In this work, we identified a novel role of the pro-tumorigenic cytokine B-cell activating factor (BAFF) in its pathophysiology. First, we observed that patients who experienced CAR-T cell-related CRS have elevated serum BAFF levels that coincide with elevated IL-6. Mechanistically, we show that IFN-γ, produced by activated CAR-T cells, stimulates monocytes to release BAFF, which induces the expression of CRS-related cytokines from monocytes. Monocytes derived from CRS patients express BCMA, which is further induced by IFN-γ stimulation. Neutralization of BAFF with belimumab significantly reduces production of various CRS and Immune Effector Cell-Associated Neurotoxicity Syndrome (ICANS)-related cytokines without impairing CAR-T cell activation or killing. Overall, we demonstrate that BAFF contributes to CAR-T-cell-related CRS, and its neutralization may be a novel strategy for treating both CRS and ICANS.

title: Spatial proteomics identifies stromal FAP-α as a predictive biomarker for therapeutic efficacy in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Lenvatinib plus PD-1 inhibitor combination therapy has emerged as a frontline treatment for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but substantial interpatient variability in therapeutic responses underscores the urgent need for reliable predictive biomarkers. Here, we enrolled 86 HCC patients treated with lenvatinib plus tislelizumab and integrated digital spatial profiling (DSP), multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF), and immunohistochemistry (IHC) to dissect intratumoral heterogeneity and identify spatially resolved biomarkers associated with treatment outcomes. DSP analysis demonstrated distinct molecular features between epithelial cell-enriched (EP-enriched) and immune cell-enriched (IM-enriched) regions, effectively capturing spatial intratumoral heterogeneity in HCC. Furthermore, we found that FAP-α expression was significantly elevated in non-responders, predominantly localized to IM-enriched regions, and correlated with M2-type macrophage infiltration accompanied by suppressed T cell infiltration. Using an mIF validation cohort of 22 patients, we confirmed that FAP-α outperformed immune cell markers as a prognostic biomarker. IHC validation in 54 patients revealed FAP-α+ cell proportion as a robust predictor (sensitivity: 80%; specificity: 71.4%), with 85.7% of patients above the optimal threshold exhibiting treatment non-response. Upregulation of FAP-α during HCC progression and association with shorter overall survival were also observed by using public data analysis. Collectively, leveraging large clinical cohorts and cross-validation across multiple technologies, we systematically dissected the spatial molecular landscape of HCC and identified FAP-α as a clinically translatable biomarker for lenvatinib plus PD-1 inhibitor therapy, providing a rationale for clinical patient stratification and guiding personalized treatment strategies.

title: Epithelial–mesenchymal transition in immune escape and immunotherapy resistance of lung cancer
abstract: Epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) drives immunotherapy resistance in lung cancer through three interconnected axes: antigen/checkpoint dysregulation, chemokine remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming. We highlight partial EMT (pEMT) as a clinically prevalent hybrid state and biomarker candidate, and metabolic rewiring as an actionable immunometabolic vulnerability. EMT signatures may complement programmed death receptor ligand-1 (PD‑L1), but require treatment-by-biomarker interaction testing. Integrating these axes enables resistance-subtype stratification and precision combination therapy.

title: Armoring STEAP1 CAR T cells with IL-18 potentiates antitumor activity in Ewing sarcoma
abstract: Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is an aggressive malignancy of children, adolescents, and young adults driven by the EWS::FLI1 fusion oncoprotein with few effective treatment options in the relapsed or refractory setting. We validate six transmembrane epithelial antigen of the prostate 1 (STEAP1) as a fusion-regulated and clinically actionable surface antigen with broad expression across a series of primary EwS tumors. Analysis of EWS::FLI1 perturbation in EwS models demonstrated regulation of STEAP1 transcript and protein expression by oncogenic EWS::FLI1. Second-generation STEAP1 CAR T cells induced complete tumor regression in orthotopic models and exhibited dose-dependent activity in disseminated disease without evidence of antigen escape. Armoring STEAP1 CAR T cells with IL-18 further potentiated antitumor efficacy, achieving complete responses without overt toxicity in approximately 80% of mice at a five-fold lower cell dose where unarmored STEAP1 CAR T cells were ineffective. Notably, adoptive transfer of autologous STEAP1 CAR T cells is currently being evaluated in a first-in-human phase I/II clinical trial in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (NCT06236139) and the compelling preclinical data presented here support clinical translation to relapsed/refractory EwS.

title: Multi-omics integration constructs an inflammation-senescence signature for predicting bladder cancer progression and therapy response
abstract: Bladder cancer (BLCA) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy with significant variability in clinical outcomes. The interplay between inflammation and cellular senescence, referred to as inflammaging, plays a critical role in tumor initiation and progression. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying inflammaging and its clinical relevance in BLCA remain poorly understood. Inflammaging signature hallmark genes (ISH genes) were identified through correlation analysis using the MSigDB database. A machine learning-based ISH-Riskscore model was developed and validated to predict BLCA prognosis. To explore the biological and clinical relevance of ISH genes and the ISH-Riskscore model, comprehensive analyses were conducted, including functional enrichment, immune infiltration, and drug sensitivity assessments based on multi-omics and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Additionally, the role of SCEL, a key ISH gene, was experimentally validated through functional assays. The ISH-Riskscore model demonstrated robust prognostic performance across multiple independent cohorts. Patients in the low-risk group exhibited higher infiltration of antitumor immune cells, correlating with more favorable clinical outcomes and potentially enhanced responses to immune checkpoint therapy. In contrast, the high-risk group displayed enrichment of pro-inflammatory, invasive, and immunosuppressive pathways, which were associated with poorer survival. scRNA-seq analysis revealed significant upregulation of SCEL in malignant epithelial cells, suggesting its role in tumor progression by promoting proliferation and migration, a finding further validated by in vitro experiments. An inflammaging signature was identified in BLCA, revealing its biological characteristics and clinical relevance. Based on this signature, a novel machine learning-based prognostic model was developed and validated, effectively predicting patient survival and therapeutic responses. Additionally, SCEL was identified as a promising therapeutic target for BLCA management.

title: Current controversies and challenges in unresectable stage III NSCLC
abstract: Unresectable stage III NSCLC is clinically heterogeneous and therapeutically challenging. Although the PACIFIC regimen defines the current standard of care, more than half of patients fail to achieve long-term control. Concurrent immunotherapy with chemoradiotherapy has not proven superior to standard consolidation, while induction, surgical conversion, and de-escalation strategies remain insufficiently validated. This review critically appraises these controversies, molecular stratification, and the key questions future trials must address.

title: The genomic and proteomic landscape of Chinese familial prostate cancer reveals unique mutational signatures and targetable pathways
abstract: Prostate cancer in Chinese men presents distinct molecular features compared with Western populations, yet the genomic basis of familial cases remains poorly defined. Here, we present the first integrated genomic and proteomic profile of 108 Chinese familial prostate cancers versus matched sporadic controls. Familial tumors exhibited a substantially higher mutational burden, driven by FOXA1 in-frame deletions within the forkhead domain—an ethnic-specific hallmark—alongside a mismatch repair–deficient signature (COSMIC 15). Copy-number profiling revealed oncogene amplifications (MYC, PIK3CA) co-occurring with deletion of tumor suppressors (PTEN, RB1). Pathway-level analysis uncovered paradoxical AR signaling (high mutation load but reduced protein abundance), concordant RAS pathway hyperactivation, and NOTCH/Wnt mutational enrichment without proteomic change. Quantitative proteomics identified 303 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs), implicating energy metabolism reprogramming and RNA splicing dysregulation. These findings define lineage-specific vulnerabilities, providing a framework for precision risk assessment and targeted interventions in high-risk Chinese families.

title: Multicentre validation of BRCAura, an AI-based histology model predicting germline BRCA1/2 mutations in HR+/HER2− breast cancer
abstract: Germline BRCA1/2 alterations (gBRCAm) are actionable drivers of breast cancer management, yet testing strategies based on clinical and family-history criteria miss many carriers. We developed BRCAura, a deep learning model that predicts gBRCAm status directly from routine histology whole-slide images. The model was externally validated in a retrospective multicentre cohort of 1025 patients with early-stage hormone receptor-positive (HR+), Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2−) breast cancer across six centres. BRCAura achieved area under the curve values of 0.81 for resections and 0.82 for biopsies, maintaining >93% sensitivity at a specificity of approximately 40%, consistent with its intended high-sensitivity rule-out design, while ruling out approximately one third of wild-type cases. Performance was robust across staining protocols and scanners and significantly exceeded established clinical and family-history models. Phenotype analysis revealed enrichment of immune infiltration and increased tumour cellularity in mutation-associated regions. These findings suggest BRCAura could help streamline germline testing pathways by optimising sequencing allocation and enabling efficient histology-based pre-screening.

title: Intratumoral co-activation of ERV transcription and RNA virus-sensing is associated with radiotherapy-induced immune response and abscopal effect
abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) transforms tumors into in situ vaccines that trigger antitumor immunity. However, the relevant pathways remain largely unelucidated, limiting clinical translation. Herein, we developed a hybrid dry-lab/wet-lab approach integrating systems-level immune phenotypes following homogenous or spatially fractionated RT (SFRT) with transcriptomic profiling of irradiated tumors. By combining feature extraction with machine-learning, including multilayer perceptron modeling, we ranked predictors of immune infiltration and patient survivability for each RT type. RT induced coordinated upregulation of viral RNA-binding proteins (OASes and RIG I-like receptors) along with endogenous retrovirus (ERV) RNAs predominately 400–800 bp long, which may serve as their ligands. During abscopal responses, OASes and ERV transcripts were co-induced and shared between irradiated and distant tumors. SFRT triggered earlier activation of OAS signaling versus homogenous RT. Our findings highlight ERVs as underappreciated contributors to RT-induced antitumor immunity and their interactions with intratumoral cytosolic sensors as potential novel biomarkers in precision radio-oncology.

title: Towards a structure-aware multi-hop retrieval framework for large language model reasoning over complex oncology guidelines
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) augmented with clinical guidelines show promise in medical question answering, yet structural parsing and evidence retrieval over complex guidelines remain challenging. We propose SMART-RAG (Structure-aware Multi-hop Augmented Retrieval Technique for RAG), a structure-aware multi-hop retrieval framework for National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines. SMART-RAG integrates automated structural parsing, structured chunking with metadata, structure-aware reranking, and multi-hop retrieval to handle flowcharts, tables, annotations, and cross-references with dynamic cross-page and cross-guideline evidence tracing. We systematically evaluated SMART-RAG on both choice and free-response oncology benchmarks constructed from public and manually curated datasets. Results showed that, conventional RAG was susceptible to retrieval noise, which could lead to erroneous prediction shifts in up to 20.69% of originally correct questions. In contrast, SMART-RAG achieved more stable performance improvements, increasing accuracy by 14.02% while reducing retrieval interference by 11.17%. Ablation studies further confirmed the importance of chunking, reranking, and multi-hop retrieval.

title: Skill-guided agentic reasoning enables longitudinal synthesis of myeloma records at expert-level concordance
abstract: Patients with multiple myeloma accumulate hundreds of clinical documents over years of sequential therapy, and every treatment decision depends on synthesis across that history. Whether large language model–based systems can match expert agreement on this task, and where they fail, has not been established. On longitudinal records of 811 patients treated over 25 years (44,962 documents and 1,334,677 laboratory values), an agentic reasoning system guided by an indexed clinical skill library was compared against single-pass retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), iterative RAG, iterative RAG augmented with the same skill library, and full-context input on 469 expert-adjudicated patient-question pairs, with an exploratory cross-dataset evaluation on MIMIC-IV. The skill-guided agent exceeded the ceiling at which iterative RAG (75.7%) and full-context input (75.8%) converged, reaching 80.1% concordance, with its advantage widening on the most complex tasks (+11.2 percentage points) and longest records. Providing the same skill library to iterative RAG matched the agent in aggregate (79.0%) and on shorter records, whereas the agent retained a significant advantage on the longest records (+10.3 percentage points in the top decile, p = 0.017) and a numerical, non-significant advantage on the most complex questions (+5.4 percentage points). The aggregate error rate (12.2%) was comparable to expert disagreement (13.6%), but a higher proportion of system errors were clinically significant (57.8 versus 18.8%).

title: Network analysis and machine learning approach identifies HSP90-associated synthetic lethal targets and drug responses in breast cancer
abstract: Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) is an ATP-dependent molecular chaperone that stabilizes numerous oncogenic proteins involved in proliferation, survival, DNA repair, and therapeutic resistance. Despite its central role in breast cancer (BRCA), monotherapy targeting HSP90 has shown limited clinical success, highlighting the need to identify therapeutically actionable HSP90-associated vulnerabilities. Here, we integrated transcriptomic, network, pharmacogenomic, single-cell, and CRISPR dependency datasets. The major HSP90 isoforms, HSP90AA1 and HSP90AB1 , were significantly overexpressed in BRCA and independently associated with poor survival. Immune and single-cell analyses linked high HSP90 expression to an immune-cold tumor microenvironment and tumor cell programs related to proliferation, DNA damage response, invasion, and metastasis. Network analysis identified synthetic lethal/viable (SL/SV) interactions involving key regulators, including PAK1, MAP2K1, MAPK3, NFKB1, TNF, CALN1, and HACD3 , highlighting interconnected therapeutic vulnerabilities. Pharmacogenomic integration with GDSC and six machine-learning algorithms identified 26 candidate compounds predicted to be effective across 51 breast cancer cell lines. CRISPR dependency analyses demonstrated negative gene effect scores for HSP90 and several SL partners, supporting their essential roles in tumor cell viability. These findings establish HSP90 as a central regulatory hub and provide a rationale for mechanism-based combination therapies and computational prioritization of precision oncology targets for experimental validation.

title: Multi-omics profiling identifies triciribine as a biomarker-guided antimetabolite therapy for acute lymphoblastic leukemia
abstract: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) exhibits molecular and metabolic heterogeneity that limits therapeutic efficacy. Although antimetabolites remain central to ALL treatment, determinants of therapeutic sensitivity and resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the activity and molecular response landscape of the purine analog triciribine (TCN) across diverse ALL models using integrated phosphoproteomics, thermal proteome profiling, and quantitative proteomics. TCN showed potent cytotoxicity across ALL cell lines and a drug response profile distinct from canonical PI3K–Akt–mTOR inhibitors. Early phosphoproteomics revealed no consistent suppression of Akt pathway signaling, with transient activation of several Akt-associated readouts and inhibition of cyclin-dependent kinase signaling. The monophosphorylated metabolite TCN-P was the predominant intracellular active species, and adenosine kinase (ADK) was required for TCN-P generation and cytotoxicity. Proteome Integral Solubility Alteration profiling identified candidate TCN-P interactions involving nucleotide metabolism, DNA replication, and protein synthesis, associated with impaired purine biosynthesis, DNA damage, translational stress, and cell-cycle perturbation. Across ALL cell lines and primary samples, ADK levels correlated positively with TCN sensitivity, supporting ADK-dependent metabolism as a major determinant of therapeutic response. Together, these findings identify TCN as a metabolically activated antileukemic agent with broad antimetabolite activity and nominate ADK as a potential predictive biomarker for precision therapy in ALL.

title: Human-in-the-loop large language model framework for identification of cutaneous immune-related adverse events
abstract: This study evaluated a retrieval-augmented, multi-agent large language model (LLM)–driven, human-in-the-loop framework for detecting cutaneous immune-related adverse events (cirAEs) from clinical notes. Compared with the unassisted manual-review group, the LLM-assisted group demonstrated higher accuracy (F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77) and inter-rater agreement measured by Cohen’s κ ( κ = 0.82 vs 0.50), and reported an approximately one-third shorter average review time. This framework pilots how LLMs can be applied to identify immune-related toxicities and, more broadly, support accurate, scalable, and transparent adverse event data extraction.

title: Functional prediction of immune checkpoint inhibitor response in renal cell carcinoma using a zebrafish patient-derived xenograft platform
abstract: To predict individual patient responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), we developed a biologic assay for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in which whole tumor cells (WTCs) isolated from patients are mixed ex vivo with nivolumab or control IgG and injected into zebrafish larvae (zPDX). ICI response is quantified as the percentage reduction in tumor size relative to control treatment. In zPDX treated with nivolumab, tumor shrinkage correlated with upregulated hIL-2 mRNA expression and was completely reversed by co-injection of a CD3-neutralizing antibody, indicating a T cell-mediated effect. Histological examination of whole-body zPDX treated with ICI revealed a significant increase in T cells and a marked decrease in vimentin + tumor cells. The zPDX assays were repeatable and reproducible within accepted precision thresholds. We performed zPDX assays for 21 cases, which clustered into three groups; High-, Low-, and Non-responders. zPDX response showed no significant correlation with immune-response gene signatures or percentage of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs). However, gene-expression analysis comparing High-responders with Low-/Non-responders revealed strong associations between zPDX response and the expression of positive immune regulators. Non-responder WTCs retained the intrinsic ability of T cells to respond to TCR stimulation. In the four patients with available clinical data, zPDX responses were generally consistent with outcomes following ICI therapy, supporting the potential of our novel zPDX platform to predict ICI efficacy in patients with RCC and, potentially, other malignancies.

title: Urinary biomarkers in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer: translating multiplex and genomic liquid biopsies into clinical practice
abstract: Urinary biomarkers have long promised to reduce the cystoscopy burden in bladder cancer, but a persistent gap separates assay performance from clinical practice. This review synthesizes the shift from protein-based tests to multiplex, genomic, and extracellular-vesicle liquid biopsies, including minimal residual disease detection and therapy selection, and sets out an implementation roadmap spanning pre-analytical standardization, decision thresholds, and pragmatic trial design.

title: Qiling formula targets CDK5R1 to suppress enzalutamide resistance in prostate cancer: integrating prognostic modeling and function validation
abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) progression to enzalutamide resistance remains a major therapeutic challenge. Grounded in Traditional Chinese Medicine theory, the Qiling Formula (QLF) targets “Qi deficiency and blood stasis” and has shown anti-tumor potential. However, its molecular mechanisms and prognostic value remain unclear. This study integrates network pharmacology, TCGA transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and cellular experiments to decode QLF’s effects. We identified a novel CDK5R1-centered prognostic signature that accurately stratifies patient risk and correlates with immune dysregulation. Spatial analysis revealed distinct tumor-immune niches, characterized by the co-localization of CDK5R1+ tumor cells with immunosuppressive SPP1+ macrophages. Mechanistically, Oridonin—a key bioactive monomer of QLF—disrupted the CDK5R1-AR axis, effectively restoring enzalutamide sensitivity in resistant cells. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations confirmed the stable binding of QLF monomers to key targets. While this work validates Oridonin as a lead compound, future investigations should focus on elucidating the functional immunomodulatory crosstalk within the TME, dissecting the synergistic contributions of other QLF constituents (e.g., astragaloside IV), and expanding the regulatory network via multi-omics integration to include other prognostically relevant genes (e.g., PTGES2). This study bridges traditional medicine and modern oncology through systems biology.

title: Preclinical characterization and first-in-human phase I dose-escalation results with JYB1907, a novel anti-GARP-TGF-β1 complex monoclonal antibody in patients with advanced solid tumors
abstract: Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) promotes immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment via the GARP-latent TGF-β1 complex on regulatory T cells. JYB1907 is a humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody targeting this complex. Preclinically, JYB1907 bound GARP-latent TGF-β1 complex with high affinity and specificity, inhibited the release of TGF-β1, and showed monotherapy antitumor activity and enhanced anti-PD-1 combination activity in humanized mouse models. Despite binding to platelets that constitutively express the GARP-latent TGF-β1 complex, it did not induce activation. In a first-in-human phase I dose-escalation trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05821595; registered 20 April 2023 under the title “JYB1907 in Subjects With Advanced Solid Tumors”), patients with advanced solid tumors received intravenous JYB1907 (0.5-30 mg/kg every 3 weeks). No dose-limiting toxicities occurred; the maximum tolerated dose was not reached. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events were grade 1-2 elevated D-dimer (50.0%), anemia (35.7%), and increased C-reactive protein (28.6%). Pharmacokinetics were dose-proportional with a long half-life (8-16 days). No anti-drug antibodies were detected. Disease control (stable disease) was achieved in 27.3% of evaluable patients; median progression-free survival was 42 days. JYB1907 demonstrated a manageable safety profile and favorable pharmacokinetics, supporting its further development in combination therapies.

title: Gastric serum biomarkers for long-term risk stratification of gastric and extra-gastric cancers: a 26-year cohort study
abstract: Gastric serum biomarkers are established for gastric cancer risk assessment, but their utility for extra-gastric malignancies and long-term risk stratification remains unexplored. We prospectively evaluated serum pepsinogens (PGI, PGII), gastrin-17 (G-17) and anti- H. pylori IgG in 20,553 Chinese adults followed for up to 26 years. Associations with cancer incidence, all-cause mortality, and dynamic risk trajectories were assessed using Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and C-statistics. Over a median 13.81-year follow-up, 1832 incident cancers and 2634 deaths occurred. Higher PGII (HR = 1.21) and G-17 (HR = 1.09) were associated with increased overall cancer risk, whereas a higher PGI/II ratio (HR = 0.83) was associated with lower risk. The PGs + clinical-factors model showed a C-statistic of 0.757 for gastric and colorectal cancer risk, with 5.77-fold higher cancer risk and 6.95-fold higher mortality in high-risk individuals, while the G-17 + clinical-factors model showed a C-statistic of 0.610 for overall cancer, with 2.56-fold higher risk and 4.53-fold higher mortality. Risk stratification diverged up to 14 years before gastric or colorectal cancer diagnosis ( P < 0.001) and overall cancer ( P < 0.05). These findings support the potential of serum pepsinogens and gastrin for long-term risk stratification of gastric and colorectal cancers and broader cancer outcomes, enabling earlier identification of individuals at elevated risk.

title: Machine learning uncovers previously undetectable genetic deletions in cancer panel sequencing
abstract: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN-deleted and wild-type tumor samples identified focal deletions missed by the TSO500 pipeline and CNVkit that were associated with concordant PTEN protein loss by immunohistochemistry. Importantly, the model detected PTEN deletions in 33/204 profiled samples that were classified as PTEN wild-type by TSO500; 75% (15/20) of stainable cases showed absent or reduced PTEN protein expression. These findings demonstrate the potential of ML to enhance panel sequencing, uncovering therapeutically relevant alterations missed by established diagnostic methods.

title: AI-driven quantitative assessment of abdominal organs and immunotherapy outcomes across multicenter hepatocellular carcinoma cohorts
abstract: Host-related imaging phenotypes beyond conventional muscle and fat measurements remain insufficiently explored in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study evaluated associations between abdominal organ features and outcomes in 1512 patients with HCC receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy across 10 cohorts from six centers. Deep learning automatically quantified nine abdominal organs from pretreatment CT or MR images, yielding 18 volume and height-normalized indices. Continuous organ measurements were assessed using multivariable Cox regression with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction; exploratory external validation used WHUH-derived median cutoffs. The primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). In the primary analysis, organ measurements were evaluated as continuous variables using multivariable Cox regression, followed by Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Exploratory external validation used median cut-offs derived from the WHUH cohort and fixed in the remaining centers. Liver volume, left adrenal gland volume, and right kidney index were associated with overall survival after FDR correction. No continuous organ metric remained significant for progression-free survival, whereas higher right kidney volume and right kidney index were associated with shorter progression-free survival in exploratory external validation. Automated multi-organ quantification from routine imaging may provide complementary prognostic information without requiring additional examinations or radiation exposure.

title: Tumor-informed molecular residual disease in resected mucosal and cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas of the head and neck
abstract: Patients with resected mucosal (HNSCC) or cutaneous (cSCC) squamous carcinomas of the head and neck undergo adjuvant therapy based on clinicopathologic prognosticators. Most patients are overtreated or undertreated, with substantial morbidity from locoregional recurrences and locoregional therapies. It is unknown whether postoperative ctDNA molecular residual disease (MRD) testing could improve patient selection. We conducted an institutional cohort study of 110 consecutive patients with non-metastatic cSCC or HPV-negative HNSCC who underwent prospectively-tested tumor-informed ctDNA testing after curative-intent resection. We hypothesized that MRD positivity before adjuvant therapy would be prognostic and predictive. After 34 months median follow-up, the sensitivity and specificity of a single detectable MRD ctDNA before adjuvant therapy were 71.0% and 85.1%, respectively. Detectable MRD was associated with inferior overall survival, locoregional recurrence, and distant metastasis. Among patients with detectable postoperative MRD, 37.5% cleared ctDNA after adjuvant therapy and had an intermediate prognosis. Detectable MRD outperformed clinicopathologic prognosticators and was predictive for adjuvant chemotherapy benefit. Patients with CCND1/CTTN amplification or CDKN2A/CDKN2B/MTAP deletions had high rates of MRD positivity (60%), were less likely to experience ctDNA clearance during adjuvant therapy (17% vs. 54%), and had inferior 24-month DFS (30.0% vs 61.7%). These findings inform the design of biomarker-adapted clinical trials.

title: Targeting NDUFS2-mediated mitochondrial hyperfunction disrupts energy homeostasis and Akt-mTOR signaling in NSCLC
abstract: This study investigates the role of NDUFS2 in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The bioinformatics analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) elucidated upregulation of NDUFS2 expression in NSCLC tissues relative to normal counterparts, correlating with unfavorable clinicopathological parameters. The single-cell RNA sequencing data further show NDUFS2 enrichment within malignant cancer cell populations across diverse primary NSCLC tumors and their metastatic sites. Validation studies employing local patient tissues and various NSCLC cell types corroborated the increased NDUFS2 expression observed in cancerous cells. NDUFS2 silencing or knockout induced profound mitochondrial dysfunction, and curtailed NSCLC cell viability, proliferation, migration, and invasion. These adverse cellular outcomes were partially mitigated by exogenous glucose or the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine. Conversely, forced overexpression of NDUFS2 enhanced mitochondrial function and augmented malignant characteristics. NDUFS2 was identified as a positive regulator of Akt-mTOR signaling pathway. The in vivo xenograft models showed that AAV-mediated NDUFS2 knockdown suppressed primary NSCLC cell xenograft growth in nude mice. Analysis of xenograft tissues confirmed the molecular consequences observed in vitro, including ATP depletion, oxidative damage, proliferation inhibition, Akt-mTOR inactivation, and apoptosis induction. Together, NDUFS2 acts as an oncogenic driver in NSCLC that supports mitochondrial function, enhances malignant phenotypes, and promotes the Akt-mTOR pathway.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and machine-learning analysis of the STAT1–GOLM1 axis in lung adenocarcinoma and small-molecule inhibitor discovery
abstract: Tumor invasion and distant metastasis remain major causes of treatment failure in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), thereby elucidating the molecular mechanisms is critical for precise treatment of LUAD. Using bulk RNA-Seq and single cell transcriptome data, combining with multi-machine learning methods, we identified GOLM1 as a core gene associated with poor prognosis in LUAD, which is highly expressed in malignant epithelial cells characterized by increased extracellular matrix (ECM)-integrin signaling, glycosylation remodelling and invasion-related transcriptional programs. Mechanistically, we validated that STAT1 is an upstream transcription activator of GOLM1 that forms a STAT1-GOLM1 axis that triggers LUAD invasion. Candidate compounds were prioritized by computational molecular docking against STAT1 and subsequently evaluated in A549 cells. Experimental validation revealed that Compound 1 exhibited the strongest inhibitory effect on LUAD cells by regulating PI3K/AKT signaling, cell-cycle and apoptosis. Collectively, our results elucidated the significant role of STAT1-GOLM1 axis in LUAD and provided a promising AI-directed inhibitor for LUAD.

title: Precision oncology in advanced melanoma: molecular landscapes and personalized therapy recommendations from the Molecular Tumor Board Freiburg
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and BRAF/MEK kinase inhibitors have substantially improved survival in advanced melanoma; however, therapeutic resistance and severe toxicities underscore the ongoing need for alternative strategies. Here, we evaluate the clinical utility of multi-omic profiling, biomarker-stratified recommendations, and survival outcomes within a prospective cohort of 98 patients with advanced cutaneous or uveal melanoma evaluated by the Molecular Tumor Board Freiburg (MTB-FR) between 2021 and 2024. Completed profiling revealed at least one potential actionable target beyond classical BRAF V600 mutations in 83.8% of cases. Alterations in NRAS , atypical BRAF variants, CDK4/6 pathway amplifications, and DNA-damage response (DDR) gene mutations most frequently guided board recommendations. Biomarker-stratified therapies were recommended for 68.4% of patients, and personalized immunotherapy combinations for 72.4%. The treatment implementation rate was 33.8% (n = 27), achieving an overall disease control rate (DCR) of 42.9% and an overall response rate (ORR) of 10.7%. These findings demonstrate that comprehensive molecular profiling in a real-world setting uncovers actionable alterations, providing viable subsequent treatment avenues that may optimize outcomes for heavily pretreated melanoma patients beyond established standards of care. Ultimately, prospective, randomized, biomarker-driven trials remain essential to validate whether these individualized diagnostic strategies translate into a reproducible survival benefit.

title: Ovarian sex cord-stromal tumors are part of the BAP1-tumor predisposition syndrome: evidence from human carriers and mouse models
abstract: Germline heterozygous BAP1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants are associated with the BAP1 -tumor predisposition syndrome ( BAP1 -TPDS). This study evaluated evidence for an association between ovarian cancers and BAP1 -TPDS. We evaluated ovarian cancer incidence in two independent cohorts of female subjects with germline BAP1 P/LP variants. Additionally, we investigated whether the high incidence of spontaneous ovarian sex cord-stromal tumors (OSCSTs) in heterozygous Bap1 -mutant FVB/N mice was strain-specific by examining their occurrence in several other Bap1 -mutant mouse models with different genetic backgrounds. In the combined human cohort of 176 females with BAP1 P/LP variants, 7 (4%) had ovarian cancer, including 3 with OSCST. Another OSCST occurred in a patient with a germline BAP1 variant with conflicting pathogenesis, for which functional studies supported pathogenicity. OSCSTs were observed in all mouse strains with germline heterozygous Bap1 mutations (incidence: 32%–73%). Biallelic inactivation of BAP1 was observed in 3/3 human and 10/10 murine OSCSTs. OSCSTs from Bap1 -mutant mice showed marked decreases in Bmpr1b , Erb , and Foxl2 expression, suggesting disruption of pathways involved in ovarian differentiation and homeostasis. In conclusion, ovarian cancers, particularly OSCSTs, represent a rarer phenotype of the BAP1 -TPDS. Downregulation of Bmpr1b , Erb , and Foxl2 may reflect alterations in pathways amenable to therapeutic targeting in OSCSTs.

title: An individual sample predictive model to classify patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma
abstract: Using RNAseq data from the IMmotion 151 clinical trial (IM151), 7 RCC biologic clusters have been defined. Several groups have attempted to predict clusters on RCC datasets without observing the association with therapy response from IM151. We developed IRIS-RCC (Individual RNA-seq Intrinsic Subtyping for RCC; available at https://irisrcc.vindhyadatascience.com/ ), to predict molecular clusters using an individual-sample model. IRIS-RCC normalizes gene expression within a given sample using ratiometric gene expression values.

title: Functional precision genomics identifies transcriptional features of therapeutic response and drug resistance in high-grade gliomas
abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive tumors with poor outcomes and limited treatment options. To identify actionable vulnerabilities and predictive biomarkers, we employed a functional precision oncology approach that combines genomic and transcriptomic profiling with drug testing in patient-derived three-dimensional culture models to enable systematic evaluation of potential targeted therapeutic strategies. While most single-agent therapies showed limited efficacy, inhibitors targeting PI3K signaling, epigenetic regulators, and survival pathways demonstrated activity in subsets of cases. Genomic alterations and transcriptional programs provided complementary insight into ex vivo drug response. Mesenchymal gliomas were particularly sensitive to BET inhibition, whereas adaptive PI3K signaling was identified as a candidate resistance mechanism. Rational combination strategies targeting complementary pathways significantly improved therapeutic efficacy across glioma subtypes. The data reveal transcriptional context as a key determinant of therapeutic response in HGG and establish a functional genomics platform to identify biomarkers, resistance mechanisms, and personalized treatment strategies.

title: Spatial transcriptomic profiling of a rare case of rhabdoid carcinoma of the pancreas
abstract: Undifferentiated carcinoma of the pancreas with rhabdoid features is a rare and lethal variant, comprising less than one percent of all pancreatic cancer cases. Here we present a single patient case with in-depth molecular characterization, including whole exome DNA sequencing and GeoMx/CosMx spatial transcriptome profiling. DNA mutation analyses revealed a novel mutational profile in this case indicating wild-type KRAS and intact SMARCB1/INI1 alongside loss-of-function mutations in TP53, KMT2C, and KMT2D, and a Class II BRAF mutation. Spatial RNA analyses of tumor sections and adjacent pancreas revealed transcriptionally distinct cell types within the tumor and adjacent tissues. The unique transcriptomic features and mutational profile of this case highlight the heterogeneity of pancreatic cancers, even within rare variants, underscoring the need for early genomic profiling to identify actionable mutations such as BRAF that may respond to targeted therapies.

title: Tracking cancer drug resistance with longitudinal multimodal AI: from biological signals to clinical decisions
abstract: Drug resistance remains the dominant cause of therapeutic failure across targeted, cytotoxic, endocrine and immunotherapeutic modalities in oncology. Tumours evolve as heterogeneous ecosystems under treatment pressure, producing branched trajectories that single biomarkers and static baseline assessments capture only incompletely. Digital oncology integrates longitudinal multimodal data—circulating tumour DNA kinetics, serial imaging and radiomics, digital pathology, and real-world clinical streams—with artificial intelligence to model resistance as a dynamic, patient-specific process. This framework supports mechanism discovery, risk stratification, adaptive dosing strategies and biologically informed trial enrichment.
